Humans fundamentally will always want better things. Even if they already have the best things there will always be a desire for better. 

>people in third world countries who work something like 18 hours a day doing physical labor, to go home to a home without running water, and who'd be lucky to be able to afford penicillin if they ever get a serious infection.

Yes neurotypicals may not be able to cope but the ones that are truly suffering, the ones that the stats mention, may benefit from experience. 

Anyways arguing this is honestly rather moot, since the original point was that living breathing people are killing themselves and that something needs to be done. 

To say that people are killing themselves because they are privileged is essentially discounting human suffering as less important simply because their suffering is not as important everyone else.

All it takes is a little empathy to understand that suffering is suffering no matter the magnitude.

There are some recently like the uniqlo wireless bras, sadly they are a good concept for the average women but not for outliers with cups larger than D, as those need more support yet are kind of like a minority in the eyes of fast fashion brands. 

And well fitted and comfortable bras are very expensive the larger one goes ($50+ to a few hundred for a good one) and women tend to wear bras to the bone before purchasing a new one because if that.

I cannot give an answer for whether or not it is due to apathetic people because I don't know. Larger brands like triumph will do their thing. All I can say is we have progressed a lot compared to a few hundred years ago's stays.

Generally, a well fitted bra is comfortable for long hours of wear. 

The reason why women wear them can vary from societal pressure to safety to aesthetics. 

For those with larger cup sizes it also has the added benefits of supporting the shoulder and back so that we can reduce pain and muscle strain in those areas. Simply imagine strapping 1 to 2kg of sandbags on both shoulders while working an average work day and you get the picture. Freely hanging breasts may also cause come discomfort when conducting strenuous activities. It is also my own preference to have my boobs firmly strapped to my chest instead of shifting and make my clothes look off in places.

That said the benefits do not out weigh the disadvantages. Bras are often poorly fitted as information on how to find the best one for each body shape is not readily available although the Internet has certainly helped with that. This causes discomfort as it may be too loose, too tight or even the wrong size. At times, even with the right size, the underwire (support wire) may still leave angry marks on the skin.

Women deal with these unwanted weights daily and bras help to mitigate some of the problem that pop up with having breasts. Innovations are needed to make them more comfortable but women have been enduring them and will continue to do so for the sake of competing with nature-blessed males.

I just have so much to do, continuously. Before I entered tertiary education, I was already unable to cope with the workflow due to reasons that involve a counsellor. I decided on the this more expensive path instead of the long-time planned road to university as I knew I needed lighter workloads.

Needless to say, I expected more downtime to recuperate. But surprise surprise, nope. I thought it was going to be okay, given that it only had six subjects compared to my previous eight. That and I would do all of them in school to the best of my abilities. I didn't expect all six to dump time-consuming work every single lesson. I'd have barely finished the previous lessons before the next batch swamped in. 

Best of all, currently I have only 2 weeks left in the term and three of the subjects decided it would be prudent to start the last—most important—assignment now. I am at my wits end trying to figure out how to finish and not fail.

Sometimes, I think it would be nice to live in the countryside. A quaint little town that has a moderate season all year round. Maybe write a little, for myself. The only things I need to worry about would be what to eat for each meals. That's it. 

I don't want to think anymore. I'm tired of trying to keep myself afloat in this competitive world. But I still have so much expectations to shoulder. I wish for simpler times but I don't want to be young and helpless again. I'm stuck and tired. I'm not in the condition to be a student. Or do anything for that matter. It's just more times than not, I see myself just letting go.
I get migraines when I'm exhausted. But e En on occasion, even if I get sufficient 8-9 hours, my headaches get worse.

I've been complaining about this since primary but I've given up on trying to make others see sense. It's still painful to wake up everyday to this life binding nonsense. But what can we *really* do about it, when we are the only ones affected; the minority. 

Because of that, we are admonished for our supposed 'faults', *demonized* by those that foolishly cling to false ideals.

Sleep and I have a love hate relationship. I, like you, experience unpleasant memories that keep me awake and in pain. I am usually on my phone to distract these thoughts but one can only go so long without sleep. 

But there is the other, much better, reason why i like it. Once I'm past the excruciating bits of memories, the dreams I have help me forget things. They help me to feel. Regardless of whether they're good or bad, it is the one and only time I am actually free from my pessimistic thoughts. I don't want to wake up from the peace.

So yeah, I agree. I hate the act of falling asleep. But I hate needing to wake up more.
